title: Entropy-Aware Telemetry Multiplexer and Latency Slice Dashboards
creator: Lina Cho
description: Objective: Build a lightweight telemetry multiplexer (mux) that attaches entropy-aware sampling hooks to request spans and routes telemetry to downstream aggregators so we can produce fine-grained 'latency slice' dashboards and slice-aware burn-rate alerts. Background: Current trace sampling is uniform and loses signal for high-variance requests (long sequences, kv-cache-miss, rare model variants). That weakens SLO attribution and results in noisy paging. This ticket implements a two-phase system: Phase 1: in-process trace hook that computes a small entropy score and forwards a deterministic sample decision + metadata tags to the mux (non-blocking). Phase 2: aggregator + slice-level metrics + dashboards + slice-aware burn-rate alert rules and paging policies. Goals: 1) Improve SLO attribution for top 5% variance slices; 2) Keep per-request CPU overhead < 1% p95; 3) Maintain privacy by avoiding raw input capture and making sampled payloads opt-in for privacy-sensitive customers. Approach: - Add a telemetry hook at the runtime ingress that computes lightweight features (sequence_length_bucket, kv_cache_hit, model_variant, tenant_tier, entropy_estimate) and appends them as span tags. - Implement entropy-aware sampling: higher probability to sample high-entropy / high-cost requests while keeping a deterministic reservoir for longitudinal correlation. - Multiplex telemetry streams: high-fidelity sampled traces -> tracing backend (Lightstep/Jaeger), aggregated slice counters -> metrics pipeline (Prometheus -> Cortex), and low-cost logs -> long-term log store. - Create Grafana dashboards that show tail latency and error-rate by slice (model_variant, seq_bucket, kv_hit, tenant). - Wire slice-aware burn-rate alerts: compute burn-rate per slice and trigger paging only for slices with customer_impact >= medium and if correlated across metrics (latency + errors + traces). Privacy & performance trade-offs: avoid payload capture, only surface hashed identifiers; sampling decisions are async so request path latency is unaffected; add throttles to prevent telemetry storms from noisy tenants.

acceptance_criteria: Telemetry hook deployed to canary cluster without measurable p95 latency increase (< 1% overhead)
Entropy sampling increases trace coverage for top variance slice by at least 4x compared to uniform sampling
Grafana dashboard surfaces per-slice p50/p95/p99 latency and error rate with filters for model_variant, seq_bucket, kv_hit
Burn-rate alert fires at slice level and follows the new paging mapping in runbook during simulated degradation
Oncall runbook updated and rehearsed in two incident drills
Privacy: no raw request payloads stored; all tenant identifiers are hashed in sampled traces unless customer opted in

notes: Trade-offs: heavier sampling improves SLO attribution but increases storage and processing costs. We will monitor cost-per-trace and throttle automatically.
Retro-fit plan: Once stable, migrate legacy uniform sampling to mux and enable a small always-on deterministic reservoir for cross-deployment correlation.
Fallback: If trace backend degrades, mux will downsample non-critical slices and elevate only high-impact slices to maintain signal for SLOs.
